guide: Deferred cord clamping and cord milking: Certainty and quality of the evidence in meta-analyses, and systematic reviews of randomized control trials, guidelines, and implementation studies
section: ABSTRACT
summary: Deferred1 cord clamping (DCC) saves lives, so why is it not implemented more rou…
content:
Deferred1 cord clamping (DCC) saves lives, so why is it not implemented more routinely? Despite neonatal benefits, DCC is under-utilized, particularly in preterm births. Umbilical cord milking (UCM) also improves some outcomes for preterm infants such as decreasing the need for transfusions. At term, DCC and UCM improve hematological indices.
Objective: The objective of this chapter is to examine the quality of evidence for both preterm and term DCC (and UCM), clinical practice guidelines and implementation issues.

guide: Deferred cord clamping and cord milking: Certainty and quality of the evidence in meta-analyses, and systematic reviews of randomized control trials, guidelines, and implementation studies
section: ABSTRACT
summary: Methods: Key evidence, primarily from network meta-analyses, meta-analyses and s…
content: Methods: Key evidence, primarily from network meta-analyses, meta-analyses and systematic reviews on both preterm and term DCC (and UCM) from randomized clinical trials, clinical practice guidelines and implementation studies, are summarized through a lens of the certainty and quality of the evidence. Regarding the certainty of evidence, for network meta-analysis the Confidence in Network Meta-analysis tool was used, and for meta-analyses the Cochrane Risk of Bias tool and the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) were used. Guideline quality was appraised with two tools: Appraisal of Guidelines for REsearch & Evaluation II (AGREE II) and AGREE-Recommendation EXcellence (AGREE-REX).

guide: Deferred cord clamping and cord milking: Certainty and quality of the evidence in meta-analyses, and systematic reviews of randomized control trials, guidelines, and implementation studies
section: ABSTRACT
summary: Results: In a network meta-analysis of 56 RCTs of cord management strategies, DC…
content: Results: In a network meta-analysis of 56 RCTs of cord management strategies, DCC reduced the odds of mortality in preterm infants by $30\%$ compared to immediate cord clamping (ICC), including in the subgroup of infants born before 33 weeks’, both with a moderate confidence assessment using the Confidence in Network Meta-analysis tool. DCC reduced the odds of any intraventricular hemorrhage (IVH) by $30\%$ , and the odds of red blood cell transfusion by more than $50\%$ , both with high ratings on the Confidence in Network Meta-analysis. Umbilical Cord Milking (UCM) did not reduce mortality compared to ICC.

guide: Deferred cord clamping and cord milking: Certainty and quality of the evidence in meta-analyses, and systematic reviews of randomized control trials, guidelines, and implementation studies
section: ABSTRACT
summary: In contrast to the benefits shown in preterm birth with DCC, a systematic review…
content: In contrast to the benefits shown in preterm birth with DCC, a systematic review showed that at term, there were no mortality benefits and few benefits at all except for improved hematological indices. A systematic review of clinical practice guidelines demonstrated that all of them endorsed DCC for uncompromised preterm infants, and 11 more cautiously noted that cord milking might be considered when DCC was not feasible. However, only half $(49\%)$ of the recommendations in the guidelines on the optimal duration of DCC were supported by high-quality evidence per AGREE-II and AGREE-REX. Fewer than one in 10 statements $(8\%)$ cited a mortality benefit with DCC for preterm infants.

guide: Deferred cord clamping and cord milking: Certainty and quality of the evidence in meta-analyses, and systematic reviews of randomized control trials, guidelines, and implementation studies
section: ABSTRACT
summary: Regarding the uptake of DCC, a systematic review of 18 studies on facilitators a…
content: Regarding the uptake of DCC, a systematic review of 18 studies on facilitators and barriers to implementation found that almost all (12 of the 14 studies) focused on strategies such as protocols, policy, or toolkits; additionally, 8 of 14 studies used didactic teaching sessions. Only 8 of 18 studies scored high on all four domains of the Mixed Method Appraisal tool.

guide: Deferred cord clamping and cord milking: Certainty and quality of the evidence in meta-analyses, and systematic reviews of randomized control trials, guidelines, and implementation studies
section: ABSTRACT
summary: Conclusions: Compared to ICC, DCC in preterm infants conferred significant benef…
content:
Conclusions: Compared to ICC, DCC in preterm infants conferred significant benefits for mortality, IVH and red blood cell transfusion, with confidence ratings of moderate (mortality) or high. Although guidelines worldwide encouraged preterm (and term) DCC, the quality of the clinical practice guidelines had room for improvement; only half of the recommendations on the optimal duration of preterm DCC were supported by high-quality evidence. Most guidelines did not mention a mortality benefit with preterm DCC and lacked details on practical aspects of implementation. Among implementation studies, which have focused mainly on protocols, policies, toolkits or didactic teaching, quality also demonstrated an opportunity for improvement.

guide: Deferred cord clamping and cord milking: Certainty and quality of the evidence in meta-analyses, and systematic reviews of randomized control trials, guidelines, and implementation studies
section: Introduction
summary: Deferred cord clamping (DCC) saves lives, so why is there a rush to clamp the co…
content: Deferred cord clamping (DCC) saves lives, so why is there a rush to clamp the cord? In California, approximately $29\%$ of preterm infants less than 32 weeks (or with a birth weight $\scriptstyle<1500~{\mathrm{g}})$ received at least 30 s of DCC, meaning $71\%$ did not receive DCC.1 In Canada, $51\%$ of infants 32 weeks or less did not receive DCC, again with the same relatively low definition of at least $30~\mathsf{s}$ .2 Rates of DCC typically fall well below those reported for another common intervention used in preterm birth settings, antenatal corticosteroids, whose rates have been reported as high as $98\%$ in preterm infants before 34 weeks.3

guide: Deferred cord clamping and cord milking: Certainty and quality of the evidence in meta-analyses, and systematic reviews of randomized control trials, guidelines, and implementation studies
section: Introduction
summary: DCC facilitates the transition to extrauterine life by allowing fetoplacental ci…
content: DCC facilitates the transition to extrauterine life by allowing fetoplacental circulation to continue as the lungs expand after birth.4 Evidence from animals indicates that clamping the cord before lung aeration can result in a $30\%$ increase in arterial pressure and cerebral blood flow.5 Clamping the cord prematurely also immediately eliminates blood from the umbilical vein, resulting in $30-50\%$ reduced preload and cardiac output.5 Some of these benefits seen with DCC are thus not present with umbilical cord milking (UCM), which is defined as the squeezing of blood in the cut or uncut cord towards the infant.6

guide: Deferred cord clamping and cord milking: Certainty and quality of the evidence in meta-analyses, and systematic reviews of randomized control trials, guidelines, and implementation studies
section: Introduction
summary: For preterm infants, the potential neonatal mortality benefits with DCC $30\%$ r…
content: For preterm infants, the potential neonatal mortality benefits with DCC $30\%$ reduction)7,8 rival those of antenatal corticosteroids $22\%$ reduction, RR $0.7895\%$ CI 0.70 to 0.87).9 However, DCC takes as little as $60\thinspace\thinspace\mathbf{s},^{7,8}$ hence it can be completed in settings when antenatal corticosteroids are not possible due to imminent birth or when they are not available. Similar to antenatal corticosteroids, DCC also reduces the risk of intraventricular hemorrhage (IVH) .7-11

guide: Deferred cord clamping and cord milking: Certainty and quality of the evidence in meta-analyses, and systematic reviews of randomized control trials, guidelines, and implementation studies
section: Introduction
summary: Despite being effective, simple and inexpensive,12,13 frequently, DCC is not per…
content: Despite being effective, simple and inexpensive,12,13 frequently, DCC is not performed.14,15 Suboptimal rates of DCC may be in part because of the lack of awareness or confidence in evidence, and conflicting or vague guidelines.16 To address issues regarding the evidence and guidelines, in this chapter the quality of the evidence on DCC will be examined: for both preterm pregnancies and term pregnancies, which will then be contrasted with the evidence cited in clinical practice guidelines and finally, implementation studies will be examined.

guide: Deferred cord clamping and cord milking: Certainty and quality of the evidence in meta-analyses, and systematic reviews of randomized control trials, guidelines, and implementation studies
section: Introduction
summary: The primary goal of this chapter is to highlight issues that can be addressed re…
content: The primary goal of this chapter is to highlight issues that can be addressed regarding the certainty and quality of evidence on DCC (versus immediate cord clamping), which will hopefully facilitate higher rates of DCC in the future, approaching those achieved in RCTs $(77\%^{17}$ to $94\%^{18}$ ) and in some cohort studies $(89\%)$ .19

guide: Deferred cord clamping and cord milking: Certainty and quality of the evidence in meta-analyses, and systematic reviews of randomized control trials, guidelines, and implementation studies
section: Certainty of evidence in preterm DCC
summary: Among recent systematic reviews and meta-analyses examining DCC versus immediate…
content: Among recent systematic reviews and meta-analyses examining DCC versus immediate cord clamping (ICC) in preterm infants,7,8,20,21 (Table 1) the network meta-analysis by Jasani et al. $2021^{20}$ has the most robust, and hence will be focused on herein. The investigators compared four different umbilical cord management strategies in preterm infants born before 37 weeks of gestation: 1) immediate umbilical cord clamping (ICC, $<30~\mathrm{~s~};$ ), 2) delayed umbilical cord clamping $(\mathrm{DCC},\ge30~\mathrm{s})$ ), 3) umbilical cord milking (UCM, squeezing the blood in $20{-}30~\mathrm{cm}$ of intact cord toward the infant two to four times at rates of five to $10~\mathrm{cm/s})$ , and 4) UCM plus DCC (squeezing the blood in the intact cord toward the infant, followed by $\ge30$ s DCC).

guide: Deferred cord clamping and cord milking: Certainty and quality of the evidence in meta-analyses, and systematic reviews of randomized control trials, guidelines, and implementation studies
section: Certainty of evidence in preterm DCC
summary: Jasani et al.
content:
Jasani et al. $2021^{20}$ included 56 RCTs with 6852 infants. In the absence of a very large RCT directly comparing all interventions, a network metaanalysis provides the best evidence about the most effective intervention. A network meta-analysis allows interventions to be compared indirectly through a common comparison group. The certainty of evidence informing each result was rated using the Confidence in Network Meta-analysis (CINeMA) Web application that has 6 domains: withinstudy bias, reporting bias, indirectness, imprecision, heterogeneity, and incoherence.

guide: Deferred cord clamping and cord milking: Certainty and quality of the evidence in meta-analyses, and systematic reviews of randomized control trials, guidelines, and implementation studies
section: Certainty of evidence in preterm DCC
summary: DCC significantly reduced the primary outcome of predischarge mortality compared…
content: DCC significantly reduced the primary outcome of predischarge mortality compared to ICC $5.0\%$ versus $7.6\%$ , Network Odds Ratio [OR] 0.64, $95\%$ Credibility Intervals (CrI), 0.390.99, 22 trials, 3083 participants, confidence rating: moderate).20 DCC also reduced predischarge mortality in the subgroup analysis of infants born before 33 weeks’ gestation $(5.8\%$ versus $9.4\%$ , Network OR 0.58, $95\%\mathrm{CrI}0.30\substack{-0.96}$ , 12 trials, 2291 participants, confidence rating: moderate) but not before 29 weeks’ gestation, although the data were scarce (Network OR 0.56, $95\%$ CrI 0.191.66, 2 trials, 73 participants, confidence rating: moderate). No other cord management interventions reduced mortality, either overall or in any subgroup.

guide: Deferred cord clamping and cord milking: Certainty and quality of the evidence in meta-analyses, and systematic reviews of randomized control trials, guidelines, and implementation studies
section: Certainty of evidence in preterm DCC
summary: Although DCC did not reduce severe IVH (grade III/IV) compared to ICC (Network O…
content: Although DCC did not reduce severe IVH (grade III/IV) compared to ICC (Network OR 0.83, $95\%$ CrI 0.471.34, 15 trials, 2469 participants, confidence rating: moderate), DCC did reduce any IVH compared to ICC $15.4\%$ versus $17.8\%$ , Network OR 0.73, $95\%$ CrI 0.540.97, 25 trials, 3316 participants, confidence rating: high).20 Similarly, UCM did not reduce severe IVH compared to ICC (Network OR 0.85; $95\%$ CrI 0.441.42, 10 trials, 628 participants, confidence rating: moderate) but did reduce any IVH compared to ICC $16.2\%$ versus $22.5\%$ , Network OR 0.58, $95\%$ CrI 0.380.84, 10 trials, 645 participants, confidence rating: high). No other interventions reduced either severe or any IVH.

summary: DCC reduced the need for red blood cell transfusion compared to ICC $37\%$ versu…
content:
DCC reduced the need for red blood cell transfusion compared to ICC $37\%$ versus $46\%$ , Network OR 0.48, $95\%$ CrI
$0.32-0.66,I^{2}=45\%$ , 18 trials, 2904 participants, confidence rating: high), as did UCM compared to ICC $(32.3\%$ versus $47.3\%$ ; Network OR 0.36, $95\%$ CrI 0.230.53, 9 trials, 688 participants, confidence rating: high).20 No other cord management interventions reduced transfusion, although data were sparse and confidence ratings were moderate.

guide: Deferred cord clamping and cord milking: Certainty and quality of the evidence in meta-analyses, and systematic reviews of randomized control trials, guidelines, and implementation studies
section: Certainty of evidence in preterm DCC
summary: No significant reductions for the other prespecified secondary outcomes, includi…
content:
No significant reductions for the other prespecified secondary outcomes, including late-onset sepsis, bronchopulmonary dysplasia, necrotizing enterocolitis, retinopathy of prematurity requiring treatment, and neurodevelopmental impairment at 2 years of age, were observed. The confidence ratings for these results were moderate.20
In summary, the network meta-analysis suggested significant benefits for mortality, IVH and need for red blood cell transfusion with DCC in comparison to ICC in preterm infants.20 Compared to ICC, UCM was associated with better outcomes regarding IVH and red blood cell transfusion.20

guide: Deferred cord clamping and cord milking: Certainty and quality of the evidence in meta-analyses, and systematic reviews of randomized control trials, guidelines, and implementation studies
section: Certainty of evidence in late preterm and term DCC
summary: A meta-analysis by the International Liaison Committee On Resuscitation Neonatal…
content: A meta-analysis by the International Liaison Committee On Resuscitation Neonatal Life Support Task Force (Gomersall et al., 2021) examined 46 RCTs data and certainty of evidence on DCC in 9159 infants born late preterm (3436 weeks) or at term.22 DCC $(\geq30~\mathrm{s})$ was compared to early cord clamping (ECC, $\mathtt{\Gamma}_{<30}:$ s) in $33~\mathrm{RCTs}$ ; seven RCTs investigated DCC ${\geq}60$ s versus $<60~\mathsf{s}$ ; one very small RCT compared DCC to intact cord milking; three compared DCC to cut cord milking; and three compared timed DCC versus a physiological approach to cord clamping. Most trials were conducted in middle- (28 studies) or high-income countries (13 studies) and over $85\%$ of studies (41 studies) took place at a single center.

summary: Regarding assessment with the Cochrane Risk of Bias tool, most studies had high/…
content: Regarding assessment with the Cochrane Risk of Bias tool, most studies had high/unclear risks of: performance bias (as blinding was not done; 46 studies), detection bias (outcome assessment not blinded; 36 studies), allocation concealment; 26 studies), selective reporting bias; 45 studies) and attrition bias; 33 studies).22 GRADE was used to assess the certainty of evidence.

summary: There were few outcomes that showed a difference statistically, with high levels…
content: There were few outcomes that showed a difference statistically, with high levels of heterogeneity, and all of which had very low GRADE certainties of evidence. 22 Compared to ECC, DCC was associated with an increase in both hemoglobin concentrations at birth within the first $24\textrm{h}$ (MD $1. 17\mathrm{{g}/\mathrm{{dL}}}$ higher, $95\%$ CI 0. 48 to 1. 86 higher, 9 studies, 1352 infants, $1^{2}=89\%$ , GRADE certainty: very low) and hematocrit at birth (mean difference (MD) $3. 38\%$ higher, $95\%$ CI 2. 08 to 4. 67 higher, 12 studies, 2183 infants, $1^{2}=81\%$ , GRADE certainty: very low). In contrast, when compared to cut cord milking, DCC was associated with lower levels of both hemoglobin concentration at birth $(\mathrm{MD}0. 56g/\$ dL lower, $95\%\mathrm{CI}0. 21$ to 0.

section: Certainty of evidence in late preterm and term DCC
summary: Although the meta-analyses focusing on preterm DCC did not show increased need f…
content: Although the meta-analyses focusing on preterm DCC did not show increased need for treatment for hyperbilirubinemia7,8 (not examined in Jasani et al20), at term DCC greater than 60 s does appear to increase risks of jaundice requiring phototherapy. The Gomersall et al. meta-analysis of late preterm and term infants found a borderline increased risk of jaundice requiring phototherapy in infants exposed to $\ge60$ s of DCC compared to $-60$ s $15. 7\%$ versus $7. 5\%$ , RR 1. 93, $95\%$ CI 1. 003. 72, $1^{2}=60\%$ , GRADE certainty: very low).

guide: Deferred cord clamping and cord milking: Certainty and quality of the evidence in meta-analyses, and systematic reviews of randomized control trials, guidelines, and implementation studies
section: Certainty of evidence in late preterm and term DCC
summary: 22 The most recent Cochrane meta-analysis of term DCC noted that infants who wer…
content: 22 The most recent Cochrane meta-analysis of term DCC noted that infants who were randomized to receive $\mathrm{DCC}\leq$ 60 s (versus $>60$ s including until cessation of cord pulsation, the opposite comparison as in the previous sentence) had slightly lower hemoglobin concentrations (DCC up to 60 s versus longer MD $-1. 49\mathrm{g}/\mathrm{dL}$ , $95\%$ CI 1. 78 to $-1. 21\mathrm{g}/\mathrm{dL})$ ) but significantly lower risk of jaundice requiring phototherapy (RR 0. 62, $95\%$ CI 0. 41 to 0. 96). Quality was reported overall for the meta-analysis as “moderate to high” but no details were provided on the tool used to assess it or results for any individual result from this meta-analysis published in 2014, when reporting standards were different. 23

guide: Deferred cord clamping and cord milking: Certainty and quality of the evidence in meta-analyses, and systematic reviews of randomized control trials, guidelines, and implementation studies
section: Quality of clinical practice guidelines on DCC
summary: To create more effective guidelines that enable better implementation of DCC, a …
content: To create more effective guidelines that enable better implementation of DCC, a systematic review by Liyanage et al. 2020 evaluating Guidelines on Deferred Cord Clamping and Cord Milking (Fig. 1) is informative.24 Based on searches of 10 academic and guideline databases, a total of 44 guideline documents or statements were identified, that had no geographic restrictions, but were mainly published from high-income countries.

guide: Deferred cord clamping and cord milking: Certainty and quality of the evidence in meta-analyses, and systematic reviews of randomized control trials, guidelines, and implementation studies
section: Quality of clinical practice guidelines on DCC
summary: While all guidelines agreed that DCC should be offered to stable preterm and ter…
content: While all guidelines agreed that DCC should be offered to stable preterm and term infants, the first major challenge was the discordance between the recommended duration in the guidelines and the actual duration of DCC in the evidence cited by the guidelines. 24 In approximately one in five recommendations (9 of 51 recommendations), the duration of DCC advocated in the guideline was not concordant with the duration in the reference cited. Other problems identified in the appraisal of the recommendations were that no sources of evidence were cited to support the suggested duration in more than one in five recommendations (11 of 51 recommendations), and $12\%$ (6 of 51 recommendations) cited other guidelines rather than primary research sources.

guide: Deferred cord clamping and cord milking: Certainty and quality of the evidence in meta-analyses, and systematic reviews of randomized control trials, guidelines, and implementation studies
section: Quality of clinical practice guidelines on DCC
summary: The recommendations for UCM were more cautious than those on DCC, with more than…
content: The recommendations for UCM were more cautious than those on DCC, with more than half (13 of 20 statements) discouraging it. Consensus on the duration of DCC, likely because most very preterm infants require some early respiratory support, and an optimal time to clamp the cord, has not yet been established. Although 29 of 44 statements excluded non-vigorous infants who required immediate resuscitation from receiving DCC, ongoing research on initiating respiratory support during DCC will address fundamental gaps in available data to support evidence-based medicine.

guide: Deferred cord clamping and cord milking: Certainty and quality of the evidence in meta-analyses, and systematic reviews of randomized control trials, guidelines, and implementation studies
section: Quality of clinical practice guidelines on DCC
summary: A second major challenge with the guidelines in relation to evidence was that th…
content: A second major challenge with the guidelines in relation to evidence was that they frequently failed to cite the most compelling evidence for DCC (i.e. reductions in mortality in preterm infants) and less compelling evidence was noted.24 Fewer than one in 10 statements cited mortality data to justify DCC.24

guide: Deferred cord clamping and cord milking: Certainty and quality of the evidence in meta-analyses, and systematic reviews of randomized control trials, guidelines, and implementation studies
section: Quality of clinical practice guidelines on DCC
summary: This systematic review showed that there is room for improvement in the quality …
content: This systematic review showed that there is room for improvement in the quality of many clinical practice guidelines on DCC, as less than half (18 of 44 statements) were judged to be of high quality in all three domains (Scope and Purpose, Clarity of Presentation, and Editorial Independence) of a modified Appraisal of Guidelines for Research and Evaluation II (AGREE II) instrument used to assess methodological rigor. Using the AGREE-Recommendation Excellence (AGREE$\mathrm{REX})^{25}$ tool, only a quarter of (11 of 44) guideline statements were of high quality in all three domains (Clinical Applicability, Values and Preferences, and Implementability). Fewer than one in five (8 of 44 statements) had high quality in all domains of AGREE II and AGREE-REX.

guide: Deferred cord clamping and cord milking: Certainty and quality of the evidence in meta-analyses, and systematic reviews of randomized control trials, guidelines, and implementation studies
section: Quality of clinical practice guidelines on DCC
summary: An additional concern was that the guidelines lacked adequate detail on implemen…
content: An additional concern was that the guidelines lacked adequate detail on implementation: less than half of guidelines had satisfactorily met criteria in the AGREE-REX domain of Implementability (which assesses the suitability of the recommendations for local adoption). On AGREEREX, the domain of Clinical Applicability assesses the quality of the evidence review, and applicability to clinicians and patients: more than $70\%$ scored high quality in this domain. However, the domain of Values and Preferences which assesses efforts taken to make recommendations and outcomes important to clinicians, patients, and policy and decision makers was the weakest domain overall: only about a quarter of the guidelines (11 of 44 guidelines) scoring high quality.

guide: Deferred cord clamping and cord milking: Certainty and quality of the evidence in meta-analyses, and systematic reviews of randomized control trials, guidelines, and implementation studies
section: Quality of clinical practice guidelines on DCC
summary: To improve rates of DCC for infants, guidelines should clearly address implement…
content: To improve rates of DCC for infants, guidelines should clearly address implementation in everyday clinical settings. This could involve, for example, a flow diagram with detailed recommendations on how DCC should be undertaken, in preterm infants, and separately for term infants (addressing the positioning of the infant, whether medications that stimulate uterine contractions should be administered to prevent postpartum hemorrhage, etc. ).

section: Quality of clinical practice guidelines on DCC
summary: A final consideration to improve implementation of DCC is to ensure that all spe…
content: A final consideration to improve implementation of DCC is to ensure that all specialties providing care for pregnant people and infants endorse a single guideline, ideally jointly issued by the societies. Ensuring that a single guideline is jointly issued by, at a minimum Obstetrical and Pediatric Societies, will enable appropriate use of DCC. This coordinated interprofessional approach has recently been completed in Canada. 26 As well as the above mentioned societies, the guideline was reviewed prior to publication by the many specialties caring for pregnant people and for both preterm and term infants; Midwifery, Nursing, Family Medicine, Maternal Fetal Medicine and Anesthesia.

guide: Deferred cord clamping and cord milking: Certainty and quality of the evidence in meta-analyses, and systematic reviews of randomized control trials, guidelines, and implementation studies
section: Quality of evidence on implementation of DCC
summary: To further enhance rates of DCC, a systematic review on quality improvement proj…
content: To further enhance rates of DCC, a systematic review on quality improvement projects and implementation barriers by Anton et al. (2019, Fig. 2) is highly informative.27 Among included studies $(n=18)$ , the duration of DCC ranged from 30 s to three minutes. Fourteen studies addressed implementation methods (with eight of these also containing data on barriers to implementation); the remaining four studies reported only on barriers. The included studies were conducted in high-income countries (16 studies; UK, USA, Canada, and Italy) and middle-income countries (2 studies; India and South Africa) with most focused on preterm populations. The majority (14 studies) were conducted at a single hospital, with the exception of four multicenter studies.

guide: Deferred cord clamping and cord milking: Certainty and quality of the evidence in meta-analyses, and systematic reviews of randomized control trials, guidelines, and implementation studies
section: Quality of evidence on implementation of DCC
summary: Among the 14 studies that had information on implementation methods, 12 utilized…
content: Among the 14 studies that had information on implementation methods, 12 utilized a protocol, policy, or toolkit and 9 of 14 used didactic teaching sessions.27 Less than half of studies (6 of 14 studies) engaged multidisciplinary teams. Other strategies mentioned in the systematic review included simulation training (3 studies), knowledge reminders such as newsletters (3 studies), and seminars (3 studies). The two most common evaluation methods included an audit post implementation (8 studies) and assessment of the pre- and post-intervention outcomes (7 studies). One of the included studies, a quality improvement study by Aziz et al. (2012) ,28 found that monthly compliance ranged from $18\%$ to as high as $93\%$ ; although in other studies $60-70\%$ compliance was more typical.27

guide: Deferred cord clamping and cord milking: Certainty and quality of the evidence in meta-analyses, and systematic reviews of randomized control trials, guidelines, and implementation studies
section: Quality of evidence on implementation of DCC
summary: Anton et al’s (2019) systematic review identified several barriers to DCC implem…
content: Anton et al’s (2019) systematic review identified several barriers to DCC implementation and practice. 27 Among the 12 studies that had information on barriers, staff knowledge (5 studies) and professional resistance to change (5 studies; i. e. , existing routines, anxiety, fixed beliefs) were the most reported barriers. 27 Postpartum hemorrhage and Cesarean section were some of the concerns voiced by obstetricians (3 studies), while pediatricians raised concerns regarding neonatal safety/need for resuscitation (5 studies) and jaundice (3 studies). An environmental challenge identified within the review was logistics (3 studies; i. e. , equipment/practical procedures).

summary: The two most frequently mentioned strategies to overcome barriers were adopting …
content: The two most frequently mentioned strategies to overcome barriers were adopting a multidisciplinary team approach $57\%$ of studies) and improved preparedness for delivery ( $43\%$ of studies). Strategies evaluated to improve compliance included education $58\%$ of studies), creation and promotion of a DCC protocol $50\%$ of studies), and audit/data collection and feedback $33\%$ of studies). Change may be gradual, as noted by a retrospective cohort study by Liu et al. (2017), which found that over the span of two years, their protocol uptake increased progressively because of continued practitioner education. 29 In summary, the systematic review by Anton et al.

section: Quality of evidence on implementation of DCC
summary: The Mixed Method Appraisal tool (MMAT) was used to assess the quality of include…
content: The Mixed Method Appraisal tool (MMAT) was used to assess the quality of included studies. 30 The MMAT is a critical appraisal tool designed to assess a mix of study designs (e. g. , qualitative, quantitative, and mixed method studies), although there have been some concerns surrounding content validity and interrater reliability for the version used. 31,32 Regarding the quality appraisal, all 18 studies’ sources of data were judged to be relevant to the research question and all 18 studies’ processes of analyzing qualitative data were relevant (method, form of data, qualitative analysis).

section: Quality of evidence on implementation of DCC
summary: However, with regard to the other two quality criteria, among the 18 studies, on…
content: However, with regard to the other two quality criteria, among the 18 studies, only 9 were thought to have given appropriate consideration to how findings relate to the context, and only 8 were judged to have given appropriate consideration to how findings relate to the researchers’ influence. Overall, only 8 studies scored high in all 4 domains. 27

guide: Deferred cord clamping and cord milking: Certainty and quality of the evidence in meta-analyses, and systematic reviews of randomized control trials, guidelines, and implementation studies
section: Conclusions
summary: In this chapter examining the certainty and quality of summarized evidence from …
content: In this chapter examining the certainty and quality of summarized evidence from network meta-analyses, meta-analyses and systematic reviews addressing various aspects of DCC, moderate to high confidence evidence showed that DCC significantly reduced preterm mortality and morbidity (e. g. intraventricular hemorrhage) compared to ICC. Although guidelines encouraged the use of DCC, the majority of studies failed to cite the most compelling evidence for it and lacked critical details on best practices for implementation. Studies addressing effectiveness of implementation strategies to increase the uptake of DCC, have focused on the use of protocols, policies and toolkits, or didactic teaching.

guide: Deferred cord clamping and cord milking: Certainty and quality of the evidence in meta-analyses, and systematic reviews of randomized control trials, guidelines, and implementation studies
section: Conclusions
summary: However, the types of study designs and quality of studies demonstrates room for…
content: However, the types of study designs and quality of studies demonstrates room for improvement of research methodology. Currently, many centres’ rates of DCC fall well below those published in RCTs and some cohort studies due, in part, from problematic guidelines and implementation methods. Moving forward, addressing gaps in the certainty and quality of the evidence and implementation interventions will enable greater uptake of DCC as a means to improve both preterm and term infant outcomes.
